compiled_state.title: [dso_reconciler/applier]: outbound CREATE+UPDATE silently no-op -> reconciler reports converged but Jira state never changes; idempotency does not converge (3 consecutive no-op passes still compute 21 filtered mutations)
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Incident Overview

The reconciler's outbound apply path silently no-ops: filter-narrowed mutations are computed and the reconciler self-reports `OK: steady-state pass converged — 10 mutations`, but observed Jira state never changes. Phase 6 idempotency disproves the convergence claim — three consecutive no-op passes each compute 21 filter-matching mutations.

Manual single-ticket isolation test on DIG-4753 mid-session confirmed `update_one → client.update_issue` with `fields_pushed=['summary','description','priority']` DOES propagate to Jira and is readable back via `acli jira workitem search`. So Jira accepts our writes when the direct legacy path is called directly. The breakage is somewhere in the full reconciler dispatch chain on the e2e probe path — likely in OutboundMutation→typed Mutation conversion, in `_mutation_to_batch_dict` (CREATE+UPDATE branching recently changed in PR #437), or in `_apply_outbound_update`'s allowlist filter where `changed_fields = payload.get("changed_fields") or payload` could collapse to {} after key-stripping.

**code_version:** e9b3fcb9e1

**Observed evidence** (from /tmp/field-probe-final-1779994025.log, b6clq8b8s task):
- Phase 1 outbound CREATE: `Phase1.verify-description-multiline — got:` (empty); all 4 `Phase1.verify-label-*` FAIL — only auto-applied `dso-id:...` label present; `Phase1.verify-comment-outbound — comment not found`
- Phase 2 outbound UPDATE: every read-back returns pre-update value — `verify-title-updated got: ...baseline...`; `verify-priority-updated expected Low got: Highest`; `verify-assignee-unassigned got: Joe Oakhart`; `verify-comment-pushed second comment not found`
- Phase 6 idempotency-pass-{1,2,3} — expected 0 filtered mutations, got: 21

**Counter-evidence** (NOT a Jira / ACLI failure): mid-session single-ticket manual test on DIG-4753 confirmed outbound UPDATE via update_one works end-to-end.

**Hypotheses** (priority order):
1. `_mutation_to_batch_dict` UPDATE branch (applier.py, PR #437 change) drops/mangles `changed_fields` during OutboundMutation → typed Mutation conversion
2. `_apply_outbound_update` allowlist filter (applier.py:304-307) silently drops every field because `changed_fields` reaches it empty or wrong-shaped; `payload.get("changed_fields") or payload` fallback collapses to {} when CREATE-side keys are stripped
3. `reconcile.py` OutboundMutation→typed Mutation conversion drops `changed_fields` before applier sees it
4. Phase 1 CREATE failures hint at related/separate bug — labels/comments/multiline description not in CREATE payload at all
5. Apply path runs against wrong jira_key — 200s on a different issue, read-back of test issue sees no change

**Affected files**:
- plugins/dso/scripts/dso_reconciler/applier.py — _apply_outbound_update (258-314), _apply_batch, _mutation_to_batch_dict, _apply_outbound_create
- plugins/dso/scripts/dso_reconciler/reconcile.py — OutboundMutation → Mutation conversion, _mutation_matches_filter
- plugins/dso/scripts/dso_reconciler/outbound_differ.py — _diff_fields, _diff_labels, _diff_comments

**Reproduction**: requires JIRA_URL/JIRA_USER/JIRA_API_TOKEN + DSO_FIELD_VALIDATION_PROBE=1; run `plugins/dso/scripts/dso_reconciler/e2e_field_validation_probe.sh` from /Users/joeoakhart/digital-service-orchestra. To localize, prefer manual reconciler invocation with --filter-local-ids <single-id> piping all stderr (probe's grep filter swallows diagnostics).

comments.body:
Audit sub-agent A (offline) — verdict: CONFIRMED, fix committed.

Branch: audit/c2-leaf-gap-agent
Commit: 04daf0a81d61a97235f4f52ef59a24988ed6b914
Base: fix/c2-outbound-update-propagation

AUDIT FINDINGS:
(a) Dispatch routing: in a full reconcile run, outbound typed UPDATE Mutations go through _mutation_to_batch_dict → _apply_batch → update_one (legacy batch, ~line 2177+). The typed leaf _apply_outbound_update is only reached via single-Mutation dispatch (apply(mutation)). The full reconcile path DOES reach update_one which has the bug 87e4 labels/comments fix.

(b) Typed-leaf gap CONFIRMED: _apply_outbound_update (lines 258-314) has _OUTBOUND_UPDATE_ALLOWLIST = frozenset({'summary','description','assignee','priority'}) with NO labels/comments dispatch. Any caller using single-typed dispatch loses labels and comments silently.

(c) Empty changed_fields silent no-op: If changed_fields={} (mutation only carries label/comment changes), allowed={}, no client call, returns fields_pushed=[] with no warning. Zero guard against this case on the base branch.

(d) CREATE path labels/comments: Standard user labels from CREATE payload are NOT added via add_label in create_one (only dso-id label is). Separate narrow gap but outside scope of these two tickets.

(e) 21 persistent idempotency mutations: outbound differ always re-fetches Jira and re-diffs. If Jira writes don't land (typed-leaf gap), mutations re-appear on every pass. No other normalization/None-value mismatch found that would independently cause persistence — the root cause is the writes not propagating.

FIX: Extended _apply_outbound_update to dispatch labels+comments (matching update_one), emit loud WARNING on empty work-set. 6 new tests, all 12 tests in test_applier_outbound_update.py pass. No new failures vs pre-change baseline (21 pre-existing failures in inbound path unrelated).

Assessment: BOTH tickets closeable pending sub-agent B live-probe confirmation. The structural typed-leaf gap is fixed.

comments.body:
fix(outbound-differ): comment dedup fix committed — commit 23705b8f51 on branch audit/c2-leaf-gap-agent.

Root cause (DIG-5287 idempotency stall 27→18→18): _diff_comments in outbound_differ.py had two bugs that caused every local comment to be re-emitted as an 'add' on every reconciler pass:

1. Wrong snapshot key: the function read jira_issue.get('comments', []) but the Jira REST API stores comments at fields['comment']['comments'] (outer key is 'comment', not 'comments'). The fetcher writes the snapshot verbatim from the fields dict, so jira_issue['comment']['comments'] is the correct lookup. Because the key was always wrong, jira_bodies was always empty and all local comments were re-emitted unconditionally.

2. ADF body mismatch: Jira Cloud v3 returns comment bodies as ADF documents (nested dicts). Without adf_to_text() normalisation, the differ compared local plain-text bodies against ADF dicts and they never matched.

Fix: read jira_issue.get('comment', {}).get('comments', []) for the Jira comment list; apply _normalise_comment_body() on both sides (adf_to_text() for ADF documents, str() passthrough otherwise) and strip() whitespace before equality comparison. Body equality after normalisation → skip; otherwise emit 'add'.

Labels (via _diff_labels) already use set-diff and were idempotent; no label fix needed.

Tests: 5 new unit tests in test_outbound_differ_comment_dedup.py — all RED before fix, GREEN after. 21 pre-existing inbound-path baseline failures unchanged.

comments.body: chunk12 follow-up (SHA 0f51601b96): The update_one field-allowlist gap that bug 85a1 fixed for issuetype/status had a sibling gap for parent. update_one's _OUTBOUND_BATCH_ALLOWLIST omitted 'parent', so parent-only outbound updates were stripped and set_parent was never invoked on the production batch path (the typed leaf _apply_outbound_update already routed parent correctly, but reconcile_once dispatches outbound via _apply_batch->update_one, not the typed leaf). Fixed by popping parent before the allowlist filter and routing via client.set_parent with a 400 hierarchy guard, mirroring the typed leaf. RED->GREEN test_update_one_parent_routing.py (4). test_update_one_field_filter.py (the 85a1 regression tests) remain green.

comments.body:
Convergence investigation (bugs 85a1/4572 scope), branch autofix-chunk12-20260603, SHA 15e417d818.

HYPOTHESIS REFUTED: bidirectional suppression does NOT block the outbound emit on same-field contention. Compute-only diagnostic (driving both differs as reconcile.py does) shows the differ seam already implements local-wins correctly: on contention (local!=jira on a field) outbound EMITS the local value and inbound is SUPPRESSED (suppression_count=1); next pass (jira==local) yields 0 mutations. Convergence works at the differ level.

ROOT CAUSE of residual non-convergence (this ticket's idempotency-churn family): assignee shape asymmetry. The inbound differ extracted only displayName from Jira's assignee field and compared it against the local assignee string. Live Jira returns assignee as {accountId, displayName, emailAddress}; local stores the email form by default. Mismatch -> phantom inbound assignee mutation EVERY pass (the field never converges). Enumerated 6 contended fields (title/description/priority/assignee/labels/status): only assignee re-emitted at the converged state; the other 5 were already stable.

FIX: mirrored outbound_differ._assignee_matches into inbound_differ._diff_jira_vs_local. A Jira dict whose email/accountId/displayName matches the local string emits nothing; a genuine reassignment still emits (carries displayName).

RED->GREEN: tests/unit/dso_reconciler/test_inbound_differ.py (test_assignee_dict_shape_matches_local_email_no_phantom RED->GREEN; test_assignee_dict_genuine_change_still_emitted guards real reassignments). Suite: 800 passed + 2 xfailed (the 1 failing test_e2e_dedup_pass is PRE-EXISTING/unrelated - FakeAcliClient lacks get_comments).

LIVE-VERIFIED against LLP-189 (real assignee shape): pre-fix 1 phantom assignee mutation {'assignee':'Joe Oakhart'}, post-fix 0. No throwaway tickets created (read-only live data used).
